question: What do we know about the generational wealth transfer, and how are these five preparing for it?

cells.label: fact

items.text: Schwab states that its average age of its client has fallen by about 10 years in the last decade and is now in the 40s, and that a third of its new-to-firm clients last year were Gen Z investors.
items.quote: Our average age of our client has fallen by about 10 years in the last decade and is now in the 40s. A third of our new-to-firm clients last year were Gen Z investors

items.text: Schwab states that industry research shows Gen Z is 45% more likely to start investing by the age of 21 as compared to Millennials, and that nearly one-third of new-to-firm retail households at Schwab this year are Gen Zers (ages 13 to 28).
items.quote: industry research shows Gen Z is 45% more likely to start investing by the age of 21 as compared to Millennials... This year, nearly one-third of new-to-firm retail households at Schwab are Gen Zers, investors between the ages of 13 and 28
items.definition: Gen Zers, investors between the ages of 13 and 28

items.text: Schwab states that roughly 80% of retail assets are held by ultra-high net worth and high net worth households, and that its retention rate around wealth transfers is extremely high, positioning it to serve future generations when wealth is passed on.
items.quote: Roughly 80% of retail assets are held by ultra-high net worth and high net worth households, and we are well positioned to continue serving future generations when that wealth is passed on. Our retention rate around wealth transfers is extremely high
items.unit: retail assets held by U/HNW households

items.text: Schwab states that approximately 70% of new-to-firm retail households are Gen Z and millennials.
items.quote: approximately 70% of new-to-firm retail households are Gen Z and millennials

items.text: Schwab states that Gen Z and Millennial investors represent 61% of new clients (per investor day marketing material).
items.quote: 61% Gen Z & Millennial Investors Percent of New Clients

items.text: Schwab states that Gen Z investors comprise nearly a third of new retail client accounts opened in 2025, and nearly 60% are under the age of 40.
items.quote: Gen Z investors comprise nearly a third of new retail client accounts opened in 2025, and nearly 60% are under the age of 40

items.text: Schwab states that 33% of its new-to-firm retail households are under the age of 30, and more than 50% are under the age of 40.
items.quote: We are attracting younger investors, with 33% of our new-to-firm retail households under the age of 30, and more than 50% under the age of 40

items.text: Schwab states that one-third of retail households who created a financial plan within the last two years are under the age of 40.
items.quote: one-third of retail households who created a financial plan within the last two years are under the age of 40
items.unit: retail households creating a financial plan under age 40

items.text: Schwab states that while client assets are more concentrated among older generations today, the average age of its clients continues to get younger.
items.quote: While client assets are more concentrated among older generations today, the average age of our clients continues to get younger

items.text: Schwab's investor day material states that 42% of thinkorswim users are Millennial or Gen Z.
items.quote: 42% of thinkorswim→ users are Millennial or Gen Z
items.unit: thinkorswim users Millennial or Gen Z

items.text: Schwab investor day material states the 2025 average age of new Retail client is approximately 39 years.
items.quote: ~39 years 2025 average age of new Retail client
items.unit: average age of new retail client

items.text: Schwab states that 61% of affluent clients ages 25 to 44 prefer to consolidate their wealth and banking relationships.
items.quote: 61% of affluent clients ages 25 to 44, so they prefer to consolidate their wealth and banking relationships
items.unit: affluent clients ages 25-44 preferring to consolidate

cells.reason: Multiple passages provide demographic trends and characteristics defining the generational wealth transfer, including age cohorts, wealth-tier concentration, and wealth-transfer retention.
